intro: To generate an image in ChatGPT on Mac, open the new ChatGPT desktop app, click the composer (the text box where you type messages), describe the picture, and send it. The picture appears in the chat, where you can open it, ask for changes, and save a copy, though saving sometimes needs a workaround.
tldr: Open the new ChatGPT desktop app, then click the composer, the text box where you type messages.
Describe the subject, setting, style and light, and say what to leave out.
Attach a reference image to the composer when you want to edit a picture, then reply in the same chat to refine it.
If right-click shows no Save option, double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it.
The exact macOS menu names and shortcuts for image generation could not be verified, so this page lists none.

blocks.text: Start with the right ChatGPT app

Open ChatGPT from your Applications folder or the Dock. OpenAI released a new ChatGPT desktop app for macOS and Windows on July 9, 2026. It combines Chat, Work and Codex in one app. The older Mac app was renamed ChatGPT Classic.
Classic still gets model updates, bug fixes and security patches. It does not get the Work and Codex agent features. Switching is optional, according to Plain AI Daily.

For image work, use the new app. OpenAI's docs describe image requests made from the app composer, and this guide could not confirm the same steps for Classic. If you cannot find Work or Codex in your app, you are probably in Classic.
Generate an image from the composer
In the desktop app, image requests start in the composer. The composer is the text box where you type messages. You type your request there, just as you would type any normal question.
Start a new chat when the picture has nothing to do with your last conversation. A separate chat is easier to find later. It also keeps old context out of the new request.
Write a prompt the model can use
A good prompt names the subject, the setting, the style and the light. Short prompts leave the model to guess. A guess can give you a picture you did not ask for, so spend a minute on the wording.

rows: a red bicycle leaning on a harbour railing at dusk
a flat, simple logo for a voice app, two shades of blue, no text
Style, colours and what to leave out
a poster for a Mac meetup, bold sans serif type, space for a date
blocks.caption: Prompt changes that usually help.

blocks.text: Say what to leave out, too. A phrase such as no people or no text tells the model where to stop. Keep any text inside the picture short, and put the exact words in quotation marks so the model knows what to write.
Edit a photo with a reference image

To change a photo or an earlier image, attach it to the composer before you type. Then describe the change. For example, attach a product photo and ask for a plain white background, with the product in the same position.
OpenAI's docs say a reference image lets ChatGPT edit the picture or use it as visual guidance. For the attach steps, read [how to attach a file in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-chatgpt).

Reference images also help when you want the same character in several pictures. Images 2.6 lets you save a photo as a permanent reference, name it, and reuse it in other chats with an @mention. That feature is rolling out in phases, so you may not see it yet.
Open the result and compare versions

Click a picture to open it in an expanded viewer. The desktop app offers two views. Focused view shows one image large. Canvas view adds Comment and Multi-select, which help when you want to mark a detail or compare several pictures.

Images 2.0 can create up to eight images from one prompt, at up to 2K resolution, according to MacRumors. Expect a set of options when you ask for variety. Use Canvas view to sort through them before you choose one.
Refine the picture without starting over
Reply in the same chat when you want a change. Name what to change and what to keep. Asking for the same bicycle with a blue frame, and the harbour unchanged, gives the model two clear instructions.

items: Keep one change per message when you can.
Describe the change in plain words, not in a long list of rules.
Use Comment in Canvas view to point at a detail, if you can see that option.
Start a new chat when the old thread gets long and the results drift.
Attach the best version as a reference before you ask for a new style.

blocks.text: Refining works best when you change one thing at a time. If several things change at once, you cannot tell which change helped.
Save the image on your Mac

Saving is where people get stuck. A 2024 forum thread describes generated images that would not save. Right-click showed no Save as option. The workaround in that thread is to double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it.

blocks.title: Saving may need a workaround
blocks.text: If right-click has no Save option, double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it. Check the file format before you send it on.
That thread is a single report with no reply from OpenAI staff and no official fix. Your version may behave differently, so check the save options after each app update.

Exporting from Preview may give you a .webp file. A user in the thread said that format would not open in Photoshop. If the app you need accepts PNG or JPEG only, check Preview's export options before you save.
The Images section on web and mobile

On the web and in the mobile app, ChatGPT has an Images section. On the web, click the sidebar icon, select Images under Search chats, then upload an image or enter a description. Storyboard18 quoted these steps from OpenAI's Images in ChatGPT help article, published December 19, 2025.
That help text covers web and mobile only. It does not name a Mac path. This guide could not confirm an Images entry in the Mac sidebar, so do not expect one until you see it.
If you prefer a browser, open ChatGPT there and use the web steps above.
Know your plan's image limits
Image limits depend on your plan and workspace settings. The ChatGPT pricing page does not list numeric caps. It uses plain wording instead, shown in the table below.

blocks.text: Third-party sites publish daily counts for Free and Plus. Those counts conflict with each other, so this guide does not use them. Check the pricing page or your account for the current wording.
Images 2.6 was released on November 4, 2026. Reports say it is available on every plan, including Free, on web, desktop and mobile.
Mistakes people make with image requests
Many image problems start with the request. A vague prompt gives a vague picture, and a long pile of rules can confuse the result. Watch for these habits.

items: Asking for long paragraphs of text inside the picture.
Sending a second request before the first picture appears.
Forgetting that a new chat does not show the older picture.
Giving up on saving after right-click, without trying Preview.
Attaching a reference image without saying what to keep.
Assuming Classic and the new app have the same features.

blocks.text: Related steps to read next

If you would rather speak your prompt, read [how to dictate a prompt in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/dictate-a-prompt-in-chatgpt). If you want the same style in every chat, read [how to set custom instructions in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/set-custom-instructions-in-chatgpt).
What the usage numbers tell you

According to Dataconomy, citing OpenAI, more than 4 billion images are generated each week across ChatGPT and the API. That volume means the image tools get frequent updates. Check the app version and the plan wording before you follow an older guide.
What this guide could not verify

blocks.title: Unverified details
blocks.text: OpenAI's Mac help pages could not be opened, so exact macOS menu names, dialog options and shortcuts for image generation are not listed here. If a button in your version has a different name, the wording may have changed since this page was written.

faq.question: Can I generate an image in ChatGPT on Mac for free?
faq.answer: Yes, the Free plan includes image creation. The pricing page calls it limited image creation and lists no numeric cap. Reports say Images 2.6 is available on every plan, including Free.

faq.question: Do I need the new ChatGPT app to make images on Mac?
faq.answer: The steps on this page use the new desktop app, where image requests start from the composer. This guide could not confirm the same steps for ChatGPT Classic. If you can open the new app, use it for image work.

faq.question: Can I make images in a browser instead of the Mac app?
faq.answer: Yes. Open ChatGPT in your browser and follow the web steps. The Images section steps quoted by Storyboard18 describe the web and mobile versions, and they do not name a Mac path.

faq.question: How many images can one prompt create?
faq.answer: Images 2.0 can create up to eight images from one prompt, at up to 2K resolution, according to MacRumors. Your plan's limits decide how many prompts you can run.

faq.question: Why will my generated image not save on Mac?
faq.answer: A forum thread describes this problem, with right-click showing no Save as option. The reported workaround is to double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it. No OpenAI staff reply appears in that thread.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for image generation?
faq.answer: This guide could not confirm one. A third-party guide lists Option+Space and Shift+Command+N, but neither is for images, and that guide may describe the older app.

faq.question: Can I edit a photo I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. Attach the photo to the composer as a reference, then say what to change and what to keep. For the attach steps, read how to attach a file in ChatGPT on Mac.

steps.name: Open the ChatGPT app
steps.text: Open ChatGPT from the Applications folder or the Dock. Use the new desktop app if you have it. The image steps in this guide are written for that app.
steps.tip: If you cannot find Work or Codex in the app, you are probably in ChatGPT Classic.

steps.name: Start a new chat
steps.text: Start a new chat for the picture, so it is easy to find later. A fresh chat also keeps the request separate from older conversations.
steps.tip: Use an existing chat only when the picture continues that conversation.

steps.name: Click the composer
steps.text: Click the text box where you type your messages. That box is the composer. In the desktop app, image requests start here.

steps.name: Describe the image
steps.text: Type a prompt that names the subject, setting, style and light. Add what to leave out. Example: a flat illustration of a red bicycle on a harbour pier at dusk, soft light, no people.
steps.tip: Short prompts leave the model to guess, so add two or three details.

steps.name: Attach a reference image (optional)
steps.text: Attach a photo or earlier picture to the composer if you want an edit or visual guidance. Then say what to change and what to keep. The attach steps are in the guide on attaching files in ChatGPT on Mac.
steps.tip: Use a sharp, well lit photo so the model can read the details.

steps.name: Send and wait
steps.text: Send the message, then wait for the picture to finish. Images 2.6 is the current model, and reports say it is on every plan, including Free.
steps.tip: Free image creation is limited, so refine the prompt before you send a second request.

steps.name: Open the image in a larger view
steps.text: Select the picture to open the expanded viewer. Choose Focused view to see one image at full size, or Canvas view to compare several.
steps.tip: Canvas view also offers Comment and Multi-select.

steps.name: Ask for changes in the same chat
steps.text: Reply with one specific change, such as same bicycle, blue frame, keep the harbour. The earlier image stays in the chat, so you can refer back to it.
steps.tip: Change one thing per message to see which change helped.

steps.name: Save a copy
steps.text: Try saving with right-click first. If there is no Save option, double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it. Check the file format before you send the file on.
steps.tip: An export from Preview may be a .webp file, which some apps will not open.

troubleshooting.problem: Right-click has no Save as option
troubleshooting.fix: A forum thread about the new Mac app reports this. Double-click the image, open it in Preview, and export it. No official fix appears in that thread, so test saving again after app updates.

troubleshooting.problem: The saved file will not open in another app
troubleshooting.fix: Exports from Preview may be .webp. If the app you need accepts only PNG or JPEG, choose that format in Preview's export options. If Preview offers no such choice, convert the file in another tool.

troubleshooting.problem: No Images entry in the Mac sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: The Images section is described for web and mobile. In the desktop app, generate from the composer, or open ChatGPT in a browser and use the web steps.

troubleshooting.problem: Image requests stop working before you expect
troubleshooting.fix: Limits depend on your plan and workspace settings. Free has limited image creation, and Plus has limits that apply. Check the pricing page, or ask your workspace admin if you use a work account.

troubleshooting.problem: The result looks nothing like the prompt
troubleshooting.fix: Rewrite the prompt with the subject, setting, style and light, then add what to leave out. Attach a reference image when the look matters more than the words.

troubleshooting.problem: Your app looks different from these steps
troubleshooting.fix: The new desktop app launched on July 9, 2026. If names or layout differ, you may be in Classic or in a newer build. Confirm you are in the new app, then compare again.
